headline: Orchestra is back in service; Travelsoft has still not said whether traveler data was taken or who was behind the attack.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read Le Figaro (s004, Nov 23): the last client was reconnected that morning and the situation is back to normal; service stays back (c004, last_checked moved). No notice on travelsoft.fr or Orchestra's news page; no CNIL or ANSSI statement found (q003, q005 open). TourMaG's cyber-attack tag shows only the two articles already cited. L'Echo touristique (s001, s003) not re-read: access blocked. Orchestra's customer page names no customers. Not eligible for resolved: last update Nov 24, under seven days.

headline: TourMaG reports the intruders got in through an old, unpatched application server.
summary: Added s005, a new TourMaG article (Nov 24; same outlet as s002). New claim c011 (Reported, one outlet): TourMaG says, from its own sources, that the intrusion came through a flaw in an old JBoss 4 application server; the company's president acknowledged the old server and said it should not have been left, but the published quotes do not confirm it as the way in. New question q006 (How did they get in?), answered Reported. c009 now covers only who the attackers are; stays Not established. c004 adds TourMaG's industry sources saying some customers were still not fully back on Monday; stays Reported. c006 adds the credential and key renewals TourMaG describes; stays Reported. c007 adds the company saying nothing critical was hacked; stays Not established. New timeline rows t007 to t010 (TourMaG's reported times). No Travelsoft notice on its own site, no CNIL or ANSSI statement and no ransom claim in the press.
